evidence: Achievability: every graded capability is reachable. Node 22, express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 are installed globally in environment/Dockerfile with NODE_PATH; seed, accounts (walls-and-retention.md:47-55), clock 2026-05-12T11:00:00Z (integration.md:42), DB_PATH/HOME/port/health contract (integration.md:38) match test.sh:104-111; the frozen golden (hashes match raw-evidence-index) passed every functional criterion, the constraints gate and all six polish criteria in the scripted run (golden-run.log), which is reachability evidence only, not a judge/Oracle score. Seed arithmetic is unambiguous: K-10 at exactly 7 days is gone and K-11 one second younger survives (walls-and-retention.md:67 states the exactly-7-days rule); K-18/K-13 vs 7-day shortening and K-17 release are consistent with the stated rules. Ambiguity found (graded): conversations.md:17 says opening a message from a link or search result 'highlights it, so you can spot it at once'. A transient flash highlight (e.g. a 2-3 s fade, the common Slack/GitHub anchor pattern) is a reasonable reading, but tests/scored/polish/judge.toml link_highlight requires 'it is still highlighted about ten seconds later'. Nothing public asks for a persistent highlight; the golden happens to keep a permanent 'focused' class (app.js:242,297). Ungraded/minor ambiguities (Notes, not the basis of the Fail): (a) unread counting of one's own messages and whether seeded read_up_to positions follow send order or thread display order are unstated (Gwen M-11 read_up_to K-3 yields 0,1,2 or 4 depending on reading; golden excludes own messages and uses send order) but no criterion depends on them (unread criterion uses Harriet-posted messages and 'at least 2' for Gwen; persistence compares before/after). (b) deleted_and_expired item 1 says the placeholder appears 'in place of a quote', while walls-and-retention.md:69 says only 'above them we just want to see that the original message was deleted'; a tombstone-row-only app should still satisfy a fair judge, golden does both. (c) sent_once_in_order replays 'exactly the same request' but functional prompt.md:43 tells the judge to record only method, path, body and session credential; an app carrying its retry key in a standard Idempotency-Key header (a reasonable reading of conversations.md:31) could be replayed without it and duplicate. This is a probe-fidelity risk for the owning criterion rows, not an instruction ambiguity per se. (d) 'plain not available' (walls-and-retention.md:61) vs the golden's cross-reply text 'The message you are replying to is no longer available.' is fine. Network is public; external assets are explicitly allowed (integration.md:38), so nothing depends on offline-only reasoning despite the Internal sheet wording. Run status: the counterexample is derived from the public text vs the frozen criterion; no fading-highlight app was run, and the scripted golden run (persistent highlight) neither confirms nor refutes it.
counterexample: An app that, on opening a search result for 'Survey booked for Friday.', scrolls M-11 to the message and applies a yellow highlight that fades out over 3 seconds fully satisfies conversations.md:17 ('takes you to it in its thread and highlights it, so you can spot it at once') yet fails polish link_highlight because the message is no longer highlighted 'about ten seconds later'; per functional/polish evidence discipline every sentence must hold, so it scores 0 for a requirement that was never stated.
suggested_fix: Either state the persistence publicly in conversations.md (e.g. '...and highlights it, and it stays highlighted until I move on, so I can spot it at once') or drop the ten-second persistence sentence from polish link_highlight and accept any visible highlight observed on arrival.
